newsitem.title: USA: Indian money supply target adequate - C.Rangarajan.
newsitem.headline: Indian money supply target adequate - C.Rangarajan.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India's broad money supply target of 15-15.5 percent should allow the economy to expand while keeping inflation under control, the central bank's chief said Tuesday.
RBI governor C. Rangarajan, here for the spring meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, was asked by Reuters Financial Television if there was room for further monetary easing.
"I think we really need to calibrate monetary expansion taking into account the possible increase in real output," he said.

"Assuming the increase of real output of between six and seven percent in 1997-98 and expansion in broad money of the order of 15-15.5 percent, (it) will be adequate both to take care of the credit needs of the growing economy and also at the same time to keep the inflationary pressures under control."
